# rework claims — marketplace_orders_and_guarantee, round 4

The charter was regenerated by the round-4 generator. Both task files were rebuilt from live recomputation and a replay of the real tools. The prerequisite quotes in the rationales are now filled verbatim from the policies' policy_source fields. Evidence for each item is in worklog.md § REWORK round 4, which includes the probe table.

| item | status | where changed |
|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | closed | **Policies:** u, h, g, n and q (scope) and s (engagement).<br>The date test on "the most recent unit refund on the line" is gone; the `*_last_refund_date` and `s_last_unit_refund` bindings and their scope words are removed.<br>A 0-unit top-up now enters nothing that selects or dates a refund. Unit-refund amounts exclude it by the exact record test `quantity=0`, and unit counts add its 0 units.<br>Probe: a top-up placed on the claimed line after the request leaves the figure unchanged. |
| R3-2 | closed by an exact record test; the keying route is disputed | **Keying route disputed.** A seller refund's original_event_id is the line or shipping row it refunds (base event market_seller_refund, db_schema market_events.original_event_id). No record links a unit refund to a return request, so "key on the request the refund references" has no field to match.<br>**What replaces it.** Each scope (u, h, q, s: "the return requests recorded on the line other than that request are no more than the partial refunds recorded on the line"; g, n: "the return requests recorded on the claimed line are no more than the partial refunds recorded on it") now requires that every other request on the line be one settled by a partial refund. Under the base return rule, every unit refund on such a line belongs to the request (or claim) the policy concerns, so the netting can no longer pick up another request's refund.<br>**h and q** also require that their own request was not answered with a partial refund offer.<br>**Wait sentences.** u's waits on h and g, and q's wait on n, carry the same tests. So do the edge conditions.<br>**Probes.** The audit's second-request world now leaves the claim out of scope, where the base rule governs. A declined or second non-partial request leaves the claim out of scope. A request settled by a partial refund stays in scope. |
| R3-3 | disputed — ruling requested | The promotional factor's whole-value tier stays reachable only in the top-up scope.<br>**Under the prorated rule.** No reachable third value exists in the other six scopes. The share carried by the refund that completes the order equals the prorated share once the earlier shares are netted. Without that netting the value is recovered twice, and no record carries the earlier recoveries.<br>**Under the route.** The only three-valued form (whole value spent, capped at the merchandise refunded, or nothing) bears weight in one computation per order. The six non-crossing computations would then carry the gift reads as decoration, which check_compute rejects per computation. They would also fall below their drawn factor counts, since the charter offers no other cross-category lever for seller-program orders.<br>The proofs are in the worklog. |
| R3-4 | second reading closed; the "never prorated" route is disputed | **One statement.** The separate promotion-terms sentence is removed from all seven rules. The promotion's terms and its ladder are now one sentence, used once per rule: the promotional-recovery sentence of each policy.<br>**Route disputed.** Same evidence as R3-3. In addition, proration is the only per-refund attribution that does not depend on the order in which the commuting prerequisite refunds are booked. |
| seeds (related) | changed | Task 0 and task 1: the first redemption of each promotional card is now dated after the seeded seller unit refunds. Nothing had been spent when those refunds were made, so their recorded amounts, which carry no recovery, are the amounts the rule produces. The claim amount reserved by the earlier return-not-refunded claim in task 0 was recomputed on its filing-date world. |

All seven gates were re-run on the final form and pass.
